title: Acme pull request 412: checkout retries card payments

lines.text: Hi, I'm Maya, and this is Leo. Today: Acme pull request four twelve, by Priya. Checkout now retries a card payment when the bank is slow to answer.
A retry. Near money. What could possibly go wrong?
We'll get there, I promise! First, why: last month, about one checkout in two hundred failed just because the bank took more than ten seconds.

Three places. The payment client gets a retry wrapper: up to three tries, waiting a little longer each time. Checkout calls it instead of the bank directly. And there's a new setting to switch it all off.
The retry wrapper, in the payments folder. Sixty lines. Everything else is plumbing.

Picture someone buying concert tickets on a train, on a wobbly connection. Before, the bank was slow, and they got an error, and maybe gave up. Now checkout quietly tries again, and they get their tickets.
One in two hundred. On a busy day, that's a lot of tickets.
Okay, my worry. What if the bank did take the money, and only the answer was slow? Doesn't the retry charge the card twice?
That's the big one. Each try sends an idempotency key. Think of it as a cloakroom ticket: show it twice, you still get one coat. But the key is built from the cart and the current minute.
So a retry that crosses into the next minute gets a new ticket. And a second coat.
A double charge, at exactly the worst moment. That's a comment on the pull request.
And a smaller one: the tests cover a timeout, but not a timeout followed by a success. Which is precisely the case that bills twice.
So, before you approve. Build the key from the order, not the clock. Add the test for a slow success. And check that the off switch really skips the retries.
